---
title: "Random walk IBM tutorials (Results)"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library('curl')

set.seed(2020)
source('../lib/ibm_functions.R')

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.cap = '', fig.align = "center", message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9.5)

# collapse each chunk's console output and plot(s) by default,
# but let the reader expand them by clicking the summary line.
default_output_hook = knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  paste0(
    '<details class="info-box"><summary>Show output</summary>\n\n',
    default_output_hook(x, options),
    '\n\n</details>'
  )
})

default_plot_hook = knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
  paste0(
    '<details class="info-box"><summary>Show plot</summary>\n\n',
    default_plot_hook(x, options),
    '\n\n</details>'
  )
})

```

This page contains the solutions to the scenarios requested in the <a href="IBM_random_walk.html">random walk IBM tutorial</a>. It starts by presenting the base case, and then changes one (or more) parameter(s) at a time. Results are collapsed by default, but you can expand them to interpret the new dynamics. Good luck!

To start, please load the IBM functions we prepared on the GitHub repository.

If the `curl` packages is not installed yet, you can do so by:
```{r results = "hide", eval = FALSE}
install.packages(curl) # install the curl library (to import data)
```

```{r eval = FALSE}
# load package 'curl'
library('curl')

# download R file with IBM function
curl_download("https://github.com/lwillem/modelling-intro/raw/master/lib/ibm_functions.R",
              destfile = "ibm_functions.R")

# load the IBM functions
source('ibm_functions.R')
```

# Base case scenario

```{r }
# you can run the random walk IBM with default parameters (see console)
run_ibm_random_walk(rng_seed = 2000)

```

# Start with 10 infected individuals (instead of 3)
```{r num_infected_10, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(num_infected_seeds = 10,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Start with 50 infected individuals (instead of 3)
```{r num_infected_50, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(num_infected_seeds = 50,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Number of days infected: 3 (instead of 7)
```{r days_infected_3, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(num_days_infected = 3,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Number of days infected: 10 (instead of 7)
```{r days_infected_10, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(num_days_infected = 10,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Population size 100 (instead of 1000)
```{r pop_size_small, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(pop_size = 100,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Population size 2000 (instead of 1000)
```{r pop_size_large, eval = TRUE}

                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Area size 10 (instead of 20)
```{r area_size_small, eval = TRUE}

                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Area size 40 (instead of 10)
```{r area_size_large, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(area_size = 40,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Max contact distance 1 (instead of 2)
```{r contact_dist_small, eval = TRUE}

```

# Max contact distance 4 (instead of 2)
```{r contact_dist_large, eval = TRUE}

                    add_baseline = T)
```

# Max velocity 0 (instead of 1)


# Max velocity 4 (instead of 1)
```{r velocity_high, eval = TRUE}

```

# Transmission probability 0.05 (instead of 0.1)

# Transmission probability 0.4 (instead of 0.1)

# Vaccine coverage 50% (uniform)
```{r vaccine_50_uniform, eval = TRUE}
run_ibm_random_walk(vaccine_coverage = 0.5,
                    apply_spatial_vaccine_refusal = F,
                    max_velocity = 0,
                    rng_seed = 2000,
                    add_baseline = T)

```

# Vaccine coverage 50% (clustered)
```{r vaccine_50_clustered, eval = TRUE}

```

# Vaccine coverage 80% (uniform)
